findings.title: User registration binds the entire request body to the User model without field restrictions

evidence.why: Binds all request fields to the User model. Model definition shows $guarded = [], meaning no fields are protected.
Model allows writing to all fields, including sensitive ones like role or owner_id.

findings.impact: An attacker can set any field (e.g., role='admin', owner_id=1) during registration.
findings.recommendation: Define a whitelist of allowed fields (e.g., $fillable = ['name', 'email']) in the User model.

findings.title: Team creation allows writing to the owner_id field via request body

evidence.why: Binds all request fields to the Team model. Model definition explicitly lists 'owner_id' as fillable.
The owner_id field is explicitly allowed to be written from the request.

findings.impact: An attacker can set the owner_id of a new team to an arbitrary user ID, hijacking ownership.
findings.recommendation: Remove 'owner_id' from the $fillable array in the Team model and set it server-side based on the authenticated user.

findings.title: User creation via extract() binds all POST parameters to the database insert

evidence.why: Location taken from the Tier 1 inventory

findings.impact: An attacker can set the 'role' field in the POST body to escalate privileges (e.g., role='admin').
findings.recommendation: Do not use extract() on user input. Explicitly map only required fields (email, name) to the statement parameters.

findings.title: User creation via **kwargs binds all JSON fields to the User model

evidence.why: Location taken from the Tier 1 inventory

findings.impact: An attacker can set any field (e.g., role='admin', is_verified=True) during user creation.
findings.recommendation: Explicitly pass only allowed fields to the User constructor or use a DTO with validation.

findings.title: User update via loop binds all JSON fields to the User model

evidence.why: Location taken from the Tier 1 inventory

findings.impact: An attacker can modify any attribute of an existing user (e.g., role='admin', owner_id=1).
findings.recommendation: Restrict the loop to a whitelist of allowed fields (e.g., name, email) before updating.
